Make a PDF with one page per photo

What this tool does

This page is set to match each image, so every page is the size of its own picture. Use it when you want the images, not a document.

Pre-set for you: Match each image page size, no page margins, Balanced (JPEG 85%). You can change it before you drop a file.

This browser cannot build a PDF locally — it is missing the image-decoding API these tools are built on. Nothing is uploaded either way. Please try a current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.

    How this works

    The PDF is assembled right here in this browser tab — on a background Web Worker, where this browser offers one: each image is fitted to its page and written into a single document, which your browser then saves. A scanned stack of paperwork never leaves your device.

    • Page size is A4, US Letter, or each page sized to its own image so nothing is padded or cropped unexpectedly.
    • Landscape images get a landscape page automatically, so a photo is never shrunk to fit the short side of a portrait sheet.
    • Drag in more images at any time — the list order is the page order, and it can be rearranged before you build.
    • JPEG and PNG are written into the PDF as they are. Other formats are converted first, because PDF does not store WebP or HEIC.
    • Nothing is stored: reloading the page discards everything.

    Most image-to-PDF tools force your pictures onto a fixed sheet of paper, which means every page carries white space that was never part of the image. This page takes the other approach: the page size matches each image, so a 3000 × 2000 photograph becomes a 3000 × 2000 page and nothing is padded, letterboxed or cropped. Margins do not apply in this mode, which is why the margin control has no effect while it is selected.

    That makes it the right choice for a specific kind of job — one where the images are the content rather than illustrations on a page:

    • Screenshots. A set of interface screenshots or a scrolling capture split into frames keeps its exact proportions and stays readable at any zoom level.
    • Scans and photographs of documents. Receipts, handwritten notes, drawings and whiteboards come out as one file that can be paged through without paper-shaped gaps between them.
    • Recipes, plans and reference sheets. Anything you would otherwise scroll through one image at a time.
    • A sequence of images that is meant to be viewed full screen, such as slides exported as pictures.

    Mixed orientations work naturally here, because there is no common page to force them into. A landscape photo is a wide page, the portrait one that follows is a tall page, and neither has been reshaped to match the other.

    The trade-off is printing. Most printers cannot print to the very edge of a sheet, so a page whose content runs to its own boundary will usually be scaled down and given a white border by the printer's own software. If the PDF is going to be printed rather than read on a screen, A4 is the better page size — it has margins built in and the output matches the paper in the tray.

    Ordering works as you would expect: pages follow the order you dropped the images in, and the move controls let you rearrange before building. The quality setting only applies to images that have to be re-encoded — PNG and WebP sources — while JPEG files are embedded exactly as they are.

    Frequently asked questions

    What does match each image actually do?

    It makes every page the exact dimensions of its own picture. There is no sheet to fit into, so nothing is padded, cropped or letterboxed, and margins do not apply.

    Why are the margins ignored in this mode?

    Because there is no fixed page for a margin to be measured against — the page is the image. Choose A4 or US Letter if you want margins around your pictures.

    Will the PDF print properly?

    It will print, but most printers cannot reach the edge of a sheet, so a page that fills its own boundary usually gets scaled down with a white border added. Use A4 for print.

    Are my photos compressed to build the PDF?

    Only if they have to be re-encoded: PNG and WebP sources are converted to JPEG at the chosen quality, while JPEG files are embedded as they are.
